root_cause.text: The rspi SPI driver used devm-managed controller registration, so on driver unbind the underlying DMA/resources could be freed before the SPI controller was explicitly unregistered, leaving the controller active while its backing resources were already gone.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `rspi_probe()` from `devm_spi_register_controller()` to `spi_register_controller()`, and in `rspi_remove()` it now calls `spi_unregister_controller()` before `rspi_release_dma()` and `pm_runtime_disable()`, with an added `spi_controller_get()/put()` pair to keep the controller alive during cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix rspi device removal by holding a controller reference through unregister and cleanup to avoid premature teardown.
intent_record.what: In rspi_remove(), the code now calls spi_controller_get(rspi->ctlr) before spi_unregister_controller(rspi->ctlr), and calls spi_controller_put(rspi->ctlr) after rspi_release_dma() and pm_runtime_disable(); these two SPI controller reference-counting calls were added around the existing teardown sequence.
intent_record.how: This change keeps the SPI controller object alive while it is being unregistered and while DMA/runtime-PM cleanup still references it, preventing premature release or use-after-free during device removal.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch controller registration from the devm-managed helper to explicit registration and update the associated error message.
intent_record.what: In rspi_probe(), the call to register the SPI controller was changed from devm_spi_register_controller(&pdev->dev, ctlr) to spi_register_controller(ctlr), and the error log message was changed from "devm_spi_register_controller error.\n" to "failed to register controller\n".
intent_record.how: The probe path no longer uses the device-managed SPI controller registration helper; instead, it performs explicit controller registration. At runtime, this changes how controller cleanup/lifetime is managed, while preserving the basic behavior of registering the controller and reporting an error if registration fails.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes rspi removal/unbind ordering so the SPI controller remains valid until explicit unregister/cleanup, preventing resources from being freed while the controller is still active.

The change directly addresses the root cause by replacing devm-managed SPI controller registration with explicit registration, which prevents the controller from remaining active after devres frees its DMA/resources during unbind.

candidates.rationale: Using the devm-managed controller registration caused the SPI controller to be automatically cleaned up with device resource teardown, which could happen before explicit controller unregistration and leave the controller active after DMA/resources were already freed.

vuln_statements.explanation: This devm-managed controller registration ties SPI controller cleanup to device resource teardown. On driver unbind, DMA/resources can be freed before the controller is explicitly unregistered, leaving the controller active after its backing resources are already gone.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this snippet. The code now uses devm-managed controller registration: `ret = devm_spi_register_controller(&pdev->dev, ctlr);` and the cleanup path releases DMA explicitly in `error3: rspi_release_dma(ctlr);` before `spi_controller_put(ctlr);`. The controller reference is stored as `rspi->ctlr = ctlr;` and the DMA channels are tied to `ctlr->dma_tx` / `ctlr->dma_rx`, but there is no remaining pattern of “devm-managed controller registration without explicit unregister” in the shown code. Since the fix is already present in the form of `devm_spi_register_controller` plus ordered DMA cleanup, `has_bug` is false and `is_fixed` is true.
